options.content:
Chronicler Dashboard

Ingestion pipeline — Kafka consumer, signature validation, transformer dispatch, SQS publish

Monitors the Chronicler service, which consumes Yoyo callback events from Kafka, verifies webhook HMAC / Svix signatures, transforms payloads through the per-provider registry (GitHub PR, Jira TCMR, Incident.io), and publishes sanitized base messages to the Scribe HP SQS queue and LLM enrichment requests to the Enricher SQS queue. Use this dashboard to track ingest rate per topic, verify per-provider transform outcomes, inspect signature validation results, watch downstream SQS publish health, and diagnose Kafka poll-loop latency.

← Unified Dashboard
📊 Historians ✍️ Scribe 🤖 Enricher & Facade 📬 SQS & Messaging 🔗 Enigmatologist ⚙️ Infrastructure
🧪 Stage Validation 👁 Watchpoint

panels.title: Service Health
panels.description: High-level service health: ingest, success, signature failures, publish failures, Kafka poll p95, and Kafka errors at a glance.

panels.title: Ingest Rate
panels.description:
Rate of Yoyo callback events the chronicler is reading off Kafka, summed across all subscribed topics (GHE, Jira, Incident.io). Orange when 0 — the consumer is silent.

`matik_chronicler_messages_received_total`

panels.title: Success Rate
panels.description:
Rate of messages that finished the full pipeline successfully — signature validated (or skipped), transformer dispatched, Scribe + Enricher publishes both succeeded.

`matik_chronicler_messages_processed_total{status="success"}`

panels.title: Signature Failures
panels.description:
Rate of inbound webhooks dropped because their HMAC / Svix signature did not validate. Non-zero here is a possible spoofing attempt or a secret rotation drift between the provider and `secret-lair`.

`matik_chronicler_signature_validations_total{result="invalid"}`

panels.title: Publish Failures
panels.description:
Rate of failed publishes to either downstream SQS queue (Scribe HP or Enricher). Failures mean the Kafka offset was NOT committed and the next poll will redeliver — sustained non-zero indicates a downstream outage.

`matik_chronicler_publish_outcome_total{status="failed"}`

panels.title: Kafka Poll P95 (s)
panels.description:
95th-percentile wall-clock time spent inside `librdkafka.Consumer.poll()`. Idle polls hit the configured `poll_timeout_seconds` (default 1s); active polls typically return in tens of milliseconds. Sustained > 5s suggests broker / network trouble.

`matik_chronicler_kafka_poll_duration_seconds_bucket`

panels.title: Kafka Errors
panels.description:
Rate of error frames surfaced on consumed messages (`msg.error()` non-None), broken down by Kafka error class. Includes things like `_PARTITION_EOF` (informational) as well as real failures. Investigate on sustained non-zero.

`matik_chronicler_kafka_errors_total`

panels.title: Message Processing
panels.description: Per-message processing throughput and latency, broken down by topic, provider, and terminal status.

panels.title: Messages Received by Topic
panels.description:
Per-topic ingest rate showing which Yoyo callback streams are flowing. Use this to confirm a specific provider's webhook traffic is reaching the consumer (e.g. after enabling a new webhook in syseng).

`sum by (topic) (rate(matik_chronicler_messages_received_total))`

panels.title: Processed by Provider & Status
panels.description:
End-to-end processed counts split by provider (github / jira / incidentio) and terminal status (success, filtered, signature_failed, unknown_provider, malformed_envelope, malformed_payload, error). The single most useful panel for understanding what the consumer is actually doing with traffic.

`matik_chronicler_messages_processed_total`

panels.title: Processing Duration P50 (s)
panels.description: Median per-message latency for the `success` path: poll → deserialize → signature → transform → Scribe publish → Enricher publish → commit. Per-provider so we can see if one transformer is heavier than the others.

panels.title: Processing Duration P95 (s)
panels.description: p95 per-message latency, success path. Watch this for slow Scribe / Enricher SQS round-trips — both publishes are sync and chained, so SQS regional latency shows up directly here.

panels.title: Processing Duration P99 (s)
panels.description: p99 per-message latency, success path. Tail-latency outliers: typically dominated by SQS publish retries or cold librdkafka rebalances.

panels.title: Filter / Drop Breakdown
panels.description: Stacked rates of every non-success terminal status — `filtered`, `signature_failed`, `unknown_provider`, `malformed_envelope`, `malformed_payload`, `error`. `filtered` is expected (e.g. non-merged GHE PRs, non-TCMR Jira issues); the others are not.

panels.title: Signature Validation
panels.description: HMAC / Svix signature validation outcomes per provider. Validates that the chronicler is correctly authenticating inbound webhooks.

panels.title: Validations by Provider & Result
panels.description:
Signature-validation outcomes per provider. `valid` is the happy path. `skipped_no_secret` appears in sandbox before `secret-lair` is populated; `skipped_no_scheme` is normal for Jira (no signing scheme exists). `invalid` should be zero in steady state.

`matik_chronicler_signature_validations_total`

panels.title: Invalid Signatures by Provider
panels.description: Just the `invalid` slice, broken out per provider, for quick alerting attribution. Sustained non-zero on a single provider points to a stale or wrong shared secret on either side.

panels.title: Downstream Publish (Scribe & Enricher)
panels.description: Outcomes of the two outbound SQS publishes (Scribe HP and Enricher) the chronicler performs for every successfully transformed event.

panels.title: Publishes by Target & Status
panels.description:
Outcome of every outbound SQS publish, labeled by target (`scribe` or `enricher`) and status (`success` or `failed`). Lets you confirm both downstream queues are accepting traffic.

`matik_chronicler_publish_outcome_total`

panels.title: Publish Failures by Target & Provider
panels.description: Only the failed publishes, split by target + provider. Helpful for distinguishing 'Scribe queue is unhealthy' from 'Enricher publishes are bouncing on one specific provider's payload shape'.

panels.title: Scribe SQS Publish Duration P95 (s)
panels.description:
p95 latency of the Scribe HP SQS publish call, measured by `SQSPublisherMetrics` on the publisher itself. Useful as a leading indicator for the message-processing p95 above — a Scribe regional slowdown will show up here first.

`matik_sqs_publish_duration_seconds_bucket{service="chronicler"}`

panels.title: Kafka Consumer Health
panels.description: Liveness and health signals from the underlying librdkafka consumer.

panels.title: Kafka Poll Duration P50 / P95 / P99 (s)
panels.description: Distribution of `consumer.poll()` durations. The p50 sits near the configured `poll_timeout_seconds` when traffic is quiet (1s by default) and drops as soon as records start arriving. Persistent p99 spikes indicate broker pressure.

panels.title: Kafka Errors by Type
panels.description: Kafka error frames per second, labeled by error class (e.g. `_PARTITION_EOF`, `_TRANSPORT`, `_AUTHENTICATION`). The poll loop continues on these but they tell you whether the broker / AirMesh side is unhappy.
